papers.title: Mapping the Trade-Offs That Shape Mammalian Brain Network Architecture
papers.abstract: A brain's wiring must satisfy conflicting pressures, from the outside world (be capable) and from the inside (stay within finite resources). These pressures often have opposing requirements. Prior work studies these trade-offs mostly between 2-3 pressures at a time, and thus cannot say how many pressures shape brain wiring or for which trade-off brains decide. To see all possible trade-offs at once and to uncover the set of most important pressures, we generate 25,000 synthetic brain networks and describe each by 29 network properties. We then place 635 human (ages 6-22) and 224 mammalian (12 taxonomic orders) brain networks in this property space. The space is triangular, and follows three pressures: computational capability, robustness to damage, and metabolic efficiency. No network is optimal at all three, and biological brains cluster in one small niche of this triangle. There, they accept higher metabolic cost to gain both robustness and capability. Development and evolution move brains in the same direction; additionally, human maturation first raises capability, and later optimizes for efficiency. This study underscores the triangular trade-off between metabolic efficiency, computational capacity and robustness, and the narrow region brains occupy in this trade-off triangle, visible only from a multi-property, cross-species perspective.

papers.title: Domain-specific and domain-general signatures of dyscalculia in computational models of behavior and parietal cortex
papers.abstract: Developmental dyscalculia is a learning disorder characterized by marked difficulties in numerical cognition, yet its cognitive and neural underpinnings remain debated. Competing accounts attribute dyscalculia either to domain-specific imprecise representations of number or to domain-general deficits in the maintenance and integration of numerical information. Here, we test both accounts in 33 adolescents and young adults with dyscalculia and 33 age- and gender-matched controls (15-23 years) who performed a sequential numerosity comparison task during fMRI. Joint computational modeling of choices and response times allowed us to dissociate perceptual and memory noise from decision variables governing the speed-accuracy tradeoff, while complementary neuroimaging analyses characterized neural number representations and their network embedding. Specifically, we quantified the precision of parietal numerosity tuning with numerical population receptive field (nPRF) modeling and derived individualized functional network maps of the same region using community detection algorithms applied to connectivity patterns. Dyscalculic participants showed greater perceptual and memory noise but also a more cautious response criterion, trading speed for accuracy to compensate for representational imprecision. Neurally, the numerosity model explained less variance in parietal cortex, suggesting less precise numerical representations, and individualized network maps assigned less of this cortex to the dorsal attention network and more to a visual network. Rather than supporting a dichotomy between the two accounts, our findings suggest that dyscalculia reflects both less precise numerical representations in parietal cortex and an altered allocation of this cortex to distributed functional systems.

papers.title: Attention warps visual-semantic representations across the human cerebellum
papers.abstract: Humans effortlessly shift their attention between objects and events in the environment. These attentional shifts modulate the representation of information in many regions of the cerebral cortex, including those that represent visual-semantic information. Based on recent evidence that the cerebellum also represents semantic information, we hypothesized that attention would also shift semantic representations in the cerebellum. To test this hypothesis, we used fMRI to measure brain activity while participants watched naturalistic movie clips and were instructed to attend to either people or vehicles. We used a voxelwise encoding model framework to recover visual-semantic representations in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum under the two conditions, and quantified the direction and magnitude of visual-semantic tuning shifts between conditions. Attention to different semantic categories had a large effect on visual-semantic tuning in the cerebellum. Representations in some regions shifted toward the attended category, and representations in other regions shifted away from the attended category. Within cerebellar regions that best represent visual-semantic information, the tuning shifts were most pronounced in Crus I and II and in lobule VI. Further, the magnitude of attentional tuning shifts was greater in the cerebellum than in the cerebral cortex, particularly for tuning shifts towards the attended category. These differences suggest that attentional modulation in the cerebellum is different than in the cerebral cortex and may not solely be driven by cerebral inputs.

papers.title: Hemispheric Complementarity is Associated with Distinct Functional and Structural Brain Profiles
papers.abstract: Hemispheric specialization is thought to follow a principle of complementarity, with homotopic functions such as language and attention lateralizing to opposite hemispheres, yet its consistency across individuals and relevance for cognition remain unclear. Using multimodal neuroimaging and twin-family data from 987 Human Connectome Project participants, we identified three sustained attentional lateralization phenotypes (right, left, bilateral) that were independent of handedness, differed by sex, and tracked broad shifts in brain organization, with bilateral individuals showing stronger intrahemispheric and homotopic connectivity. Examining attention and language revealed three multidomain profiles (crowded, mixed, split) reflecting whether functions colocalize within or are distributed across hemispheres. Mixed organization was linked to higher planum polare myelination, whereas crowded organization showed higher fiber density connectivity across dorsal attention-default network. Both phenotypes were heritable, yet neither predicted cognitive performance. These findings reveal a brain organization in which specialization emerges from flexible, heritable patterns linking function, structural connectivity, and myeloarchitecture.

papers.title: EARLY-LIFE STRESS INDUCES SEXUALLY DIMORPHIC BRAIN AGING VIA MESOLIMBIC ALTERATIONS AND FRONTO-STRIATAL DYSFUNCTION
papers.abstract: Prenatal stress influences brain development; however, its long-term, region-specific effects on brain aging in males and females remain insufficiently characterized. This study examined the impact of unpredictable mild prenatal stress on behavior, cognition, and maternal care in C57BL/6J mice at middle (12 months) and old (18 months) ages. Stressed dams showed fragmented, unpredictable maternal behaviors, creating a stressful postnatal environment without impairing caregiving capacity. Both male and female offspring were born with lower birth weights and showed rapid postnatal growth, a trajectory associated with central insulin resistance and hippocampal signaling deficits. Sex-specific behavioral differences emerged with age. Middle-aged stressed males exhibited anhedonia, which progressed to hyperactivity, stereotypy, and persistent spatial memory deficits in old age. These outcomes corresponded with accelerated fronto-striatal decline, likely mediated by insulin resistance and increased rigidity of medial prefrontal cortex structures due to diminished local estrogenic activity. In contrast, middle-aged stressed females displayed hypoactivity and reduced anxiety, later developing anhedonia in old age while maintaining hippocampus-dependent memory. In females, this pattern supports a model in which a neuroestrogen - and growth factor-dependent feedback loop transiently preserves hippocampal plasticity but compromises dopaminergic function in reward circuits. This balance may deteriorate with reproductive senescence. Both sexes retained cognitive flexibility, indicating domain-specific rather than global cognitive impairment. These findings demonstrate that excessive prenatal glucocorticoid exposure and unpredictable postnatal care produce a combined hormonal and metabolic insult, resulting in sexually divergent trajectories of brain aging. The results underscore the necessity of incorporating sex as a biological variable in fetal programming research across the lifespan.

papers.title: Developmental prefrontal myelination shapes inhibitory interneuron function and adult social behavior
papers.abstract: Early-life adversity and abnormal myelination are implicated in psychiatric disorders, but how developmental myelination influences adult social cognition remains unclear. Here, we tested whether disrupting developmental myelination in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) impairs adult social behavior. Using complementary genetic strategies in male mice, we suppressed Myelin Regulatory Factor (Myrf)-dependent myelination locally in the juvenile mPFC or broadly in oligodendrocyte-lineage cells. Both approaches selectively impaired adult social novelty preference while sparing sociability, locomotion, and affective behaviors. Focal prefrontal dysmyelination also reduced social dominance. Spatial transcriptomics revealed coupling between myelin-related genes and parvalbumin (PV) interneuron markers in the healthy mPFC, which was disrupted by developmental hypomyelination. Consistent with this transcriptional alteration, PV interneurons showed reduced high-frequency firing despite preserved intrinsic excitability. In the human prefrontal cortex, MBP-PV expression was correlated in controls but not in individuals with schizophrenia. These findings indicate that developmental prefrontal myelination contributes to PV interneuron maturation and suggest that disrupted oligodendrocyte-interneuron coordination may contribute to impaired social recognition.

papers.title: Disrupting the Right Inferior Frontal Gyrus Increases Social Brain Activity During Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Neuroimaging studies have identified a specialised social brain network that supports emotion recognition and social cognition. This network performs a range of functions that include facial expression recognition and inferring the mental states of others. Studies of neuropsychological patients report that damage to the right inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), the top-down control area in this network, impairs facial expression recognition. To investigate how transient disruption of the right IFG affects the wider social brain we combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Participants (n=20) were scanned across two sessions while performing a delayed match-to-sample emotion recognition task in which happy or fearful expressions were preceded by a congruent or incongruent word cue. Prior to each scan, thetaburst TMS was delivered over the right IFG or over the vertex control site (session order was balanced across participants). A group whole-brain analysis revealed that TMS to the IFG increased neural activity in multiple regions of the social brain network. These included the bilateral temporal pole, precuneus and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). This pattern of results shows that the disruption of top-down control mechanisms localised in the IFG alters the neural processing in remote nodes of the social brain network. Our findings are discussed within the wider context of how we recognise and understand the emotions of other people.

papers.title: rpSTS Stimulation Disrupts Shared Neural Responses to Social Content during Naturalistic Viewing
papers.abstract: Shared understanding of common experiences can foster feelings of social closeness and friendship, and help us understand those experiences. Recent work has suggested that patterns of neural activity shared across individuals, especially throughout the default mode network, may underlie shared representations. Here we used repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) and functional magnetic resonance imaging during movie watching to show that shared neural patterns to common experiences rely on the encoding of social information from the environment by the right posterior superior temporal sulcus (rpSTS). An encoding model of movie features showed that rTMS selectively degraded social feature encoding in rpSTS, leaving low-level visual encoding in early visual cortex intact. Using natural language processing (NLP)-based analysis, we found that rpSTS stimulation was associated with reduced memory and intersubject pattern similarity across DMN and limbic networks during scenes central to the movie narrative. Projecting scene embeddings onto NLP-based concept axes revealed reductions in memory and neural pattern similarity for scenes conveying helplessness and empathy following rTMS. These findings provide causal evidence that the rpSTS is a key region that encodes shared social information into common neural representations, and suggest that disrupting its input leads DMN representations to become idiosyncratic.

papers.title: A human CHRNA6 3' UTR variant alters the molecular environment and microRNA engagement of the adolescent VTA without changing Chrna6 transcript abundance
papers.abstract: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6, encoding the alpha6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the 'C' or 'G' allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or polyadenylation site selection. The variant was instead associated with a transcriptional signature spanning myelin maintenance (Enpp6), lipid metabolism (Retsat), and genomic repair (Polq), and with elevated basal lipid peroxidation in alpha6GG animals. Computational folding predicted greater conformational flexibility of the 'G' allele, and spatial colocalization of Chrna6 with miRNA-365-5p was reduced in alpha6GG animals of both sexes. Coordinated expression of the two transcripts, however, followed a sex-by-genotype pattern, absent in alpha6CC females and alpha6GG males. These same groups showed elevated tyrosine hydroxylase expression and dopaminergic neuron number, and expansion of the Chrna6 co-expression network following nicotine. We propose that rs2304297 acts through two distinct layers: genotype determines spatial engagement of miRNA-365-5p with the transcript, while sex determines whether that engagement produces functional regulation. These findings identify a post-transcriptional mechanism for a non-coding nicotine addiction risk variant and demonstrate that its molecular effect can be uniform while its consequences are not.

papers.title: Ordinal position in auditory sequences is encoded in population dynamics in macaque frontal cortex
papers.abstract: The ability to extract structure from sensory sequences requires tracking not only stimulus identity but also ordinal position within a sequence. How and where ordinal information is represented in the primate brain remains unclear. Here, we recorded activity in populations of single neurons simultaneously from auditory cortex and ventrolateral prefrontal cortex in macaques passively listening to structured auditory sequences. Population-level analyses revealed that frontal cortex activity evolved progressively across the sequence, occupying distinct regions of neural state space for successive ordinal positions. In contrast, auditory cortex population activity reset with each element, producing stereotyped, stimulus-locked trajectories. Consistent with this dissociation, frontal cortex populations robustly decoded ordinal position independently of stimulus identity, whereas auditory cortex showed weak positional decoding despite strong identity representations. Frontal neurons further exhibited longer intrinsic timescales and reduced synchronization to element presentation, supporting integration of information across multiple elements. Together, these findings identify frontal activity as a key substrate for ordinal position encoding during auditory sequence processing, while auditory cortex primarily supports element-specific sensory representations.

papers.title: The anterior insular cortex mediates higher-order threat learning and memory
papers.abstract: Learning about potential threats is indispensable for survival, and its deficits underlie numerous neuropsychiatric disorders. Human brain imaging suggests the anterior insular cortex (AIC) as a key neural correlate of threat learning, yet its mechanistic role remains unclear. Leveraging multimodal systems neuroscience approaches, we demonstrate that AIC excitatory neurons, specifically layer 5 pyramidal neurons projecting to the basolateral amygdala, are essential for higher-order threat learning/memory. They are specifically required when a predictor is temporally separated from an aversive event or when the predictive information is embedded within a diffuse context. In contrast, the AIC is dispensable for elementary, temporally contiguous threat learning. Surprisingly, while the AIC promotes memory formation, it also constrains the level of fear expression during retrieval in a context-dependent manner. This bidirectional control is mediated by the recruitment of distinct AIC neuronal ensembles. Together, we identify a novel circuit mechanism for bidirectional regulation of higher-order threat learning/memory.

papers.title: Differential utilization of PACAP and glutamate in parabrachial neurons shapes pain and stress
papers.abstract: The external parabrachial nucleus (elPBN) contributes to diverse behaviors, including pain and stress. Neurons in this region use glutamatergic and neuropeptidergic signaling, with pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide (PACAP) expressed in a subset of glutamatergic neurons. Deletion of PACAP in elPBN neurons attenuates behavioral responses to stress, but the contribution of PACAP to pain sensitization and of glutamatergic neurotransmission to pain- and stress-related responses remain poorly understood. Here, we show that constitutive loss of PACAP markedly attenuated nerve injury-induced hypersensitivity across heat, pressure, cold and tactile modalities without altering baseline nociception, while also reducing inflammation-induced spontaneous pain-related behavior. Notably, selective deletion of PACAP within elPBN neurons phenocopied the suppression of injury-induced hypersensitivity, but left inflammation- induced pain-related behavior unaffected. Ex vivo optogenetic-assisted circuit mapping showed that activation of PACAP-expressing elPBN terminals elicited glutamatergic transmission onto central amygdala (CeA) PKC{delta}-expressing neurons. Selective deletion of VGluT2 in elPBN neurons reduced nerve injury-induced hypersensitivity but, unlike PACAP deletion, also reduced inflammation-induced pain-related behavior, while leaving stress-induced hypophagia intact. Together, these findings reveal differential requirements for PACAP and glutamatergic neurotransmission within the elPBN across pain- and stress-related behaviors.

papers.title: A large, comprehensive labeled MRI dataset of the human lateral ventricle choroid plexus
papers.abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP.

papers.title: FMR1 Perturbations Disrupt Sensory Corticostriatal Circuits and Mitochondrial Energetics in Fragile X Syndrome
papers.abstract: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) features sensory, social, and cognitive dysfunction, but how fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) deficiency disrupts sensory corticostriatal circuitry and whether distinct FMR1 perturbations converge on shared cellular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. We integrated diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) in individuals with FXS and Fmr1-knockout (KO) mice with projection-defined calcium recording, bidirectional optogenetic manipulation, primary somatosensory cortex (S1)-targeted expression of three patient-associated FMR1 missense variants, regional transcriptomics, and optical manipulation of mitochondrial energetic state. Individuals with FXS exhibited disrupted sensory corticostriatal structural connectivity, with mouse analyses further localizing abnormalities to S1-striatal pathways. Fmr1 deficiency impaired recruitment of the S1-dorsomedial striatum (DMS) pathway during social interaction, and projection-specific manipulation demonstrated that S1-DMS dysfunction contributes to social and cognitive deficits. Three patient-associated FMR1 variants, I234T, E329G, and R586Q, converged on social behavioral deficits, which were improved by S1-DMS activation. Transcriptomic analyses revealed convergent oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS)-related mitochondrial remodeling in S1 and DMS across Fmr1 deficiency and variant models. Systemic treatment with the mitochondria-targeted antioxidant MitoQ attenuated novel-location-recognition, social-interaction, and social-novelty deficits in Fmr1-KO mice. Moreover, mt-EcGAPR-based Mitochondrial OptoEnergetic Activation (Mito-OptoEA) enhanced mitochondrial energetic state in S1 and improved novel-location recognition and sociability in both Fmr1-KO and I234T models. Together, these findings define a sensory corticostriatal circuit-metabolic framework for FXS in which S1-DMS circuit dysfunction and convergent mitochondrial energetic abnormalities contribute to FMR1-related social and cognitive phenotypes.

papers.title: ATP1A3 E815K Disrupts Sodium Homeostasis and Excitability in Human Alternating Hemiplegia of Childhood Neurons
papers.abstract: Alternating hemiplegia of childhood (AHC) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by heterozygous de novo mutations in the ATP1A3 gene, which encodes the neuron-specific catalytic 3 subunit of the P-type Na/K-ATPase. Among these, the E815K variant is the second most frequent ATP1A3 mutation in AHC and is associated with the most severe clinical phenotypes, characterized by frequent epileptic and dystonic episodes and profound developmental impairment, making it a key target for mechanistic study. Although E815K was shown to disrupt pump function in heterologous systems and animal models, its impact on human neurons remain poorly understood. To investigate its disease-relevant pathophysiology, we generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from an AHC patient carrying the E815K mutation and differentiated them into mature neurons. Patient-derived neurons displayed normal differentiation and synaptogenesis, with preserved evoked synaptic transmission. However, 3-specific Na/K pump currents were nearly abolished, whereas 1 activity remained intact. This selective dysfunction was associated with a depolarized resting membrane potential, reduced input resistance, and diminished intrinsic excitability. Patient neurons generated fewer action potentials in response to depolarizing current steps, displayed altered firing patterns, and showed significantly decreased voltage-gated sodium current densities, while potassium conductance remained unaffected. Taken together, these results indicate that the ATP1A3 E815K mutation disrupts intracellular sodium homeostasis and consequently modifies the excitability of human neurons. Overall, these findings provide mechanistic insight into the molecular pathophysiology underlying this AHC variant and thereby establish a patient-derived neuronal model which serves as a platform for future drug screening approaches and therapeutic investigation.

papers.title: Spoken language comprehension relies on context-dependent neural weighting of syntax and prosody
papers.abstract: Comprehending spoken language requires extracting syntactic structure and meaning from a continuous acoustic signal. Psycholinguistic evidence points to a key role for prosody in this process. However, because interactions between prosody and syntax are typically demonstrated using carefully controlled sentence constructions, it remains unclear whether such interactions constitute a general, default property of spoken language processing. Addressing this question requires naturalistic, broad-coverage data. Here, we combined experimental psycholinguistics with naturalistic neuroscience to investigate the joint neural encoding of syntax and prosody in MEG recordings of 26 participants (19 female) listening to narrative speech. Linguistic annotations revealed that strong prosodic boundaries tend to coincide with syntactic phrase closures, and that the strength of prosodic boundaries scales with the number of phrases closed. Using time-resolved regression with temporal response functions, we modeled how these features relate to delta-band neural activity during continuous speech processing. Our results reveal a bidirectional interaction between syntax and prosody. Prosodic marking modulates the neural processing of syntax, with phrase closures being encoded more strongly when accompanied by strong prosodic boundaries. Conversely, syntactic structure shapes prosodic encoding, such that boundary strength is neurally encoded primarily at points of syntactic phrase closure. These findings demonstrate that syntax and prosody are encoded not independently, but in a context-dependent and mutually constraining manner, highlighting their joint role in guiding structure building during naturalistic spoken language comprehension.

papers.title: Human single-neuron correlates of somatosensation
papers.abstract: Understanding the neural correlates of consciousness poses a central challenge in neuroscience, with longstanding debate over which cortical areas underlie subjective sensory perception. In the tactile domain, posterior parietal cortex (PPC) and primary somatosensory cortex (S1) are candidate cortical substrates for neural correlates of consciousness due to their crucial roles in somatosensory processing. Yet whether and how these regions contribute to conscious tactile perception remains unclear. Here, to address this issue, we leveraged chronic intracortical recordings to simultaneously monitor large ensembles of single neurons in grasp related cortical areas from three participants with tetraplegia while natural vibrotactile stimuli were delivered to a sensate region of the upper limb. We demonstrate that an orchestration of neural activity emerged across the grasp-related parietal-frontal network at near-threshold perception. Within this distributed network, we then focused on PPC and S1. While S1 responses closely tracked the amplitude of the physical stimulus, PPC activity covaried more strongly with awareness and confidence. This single-neuron evidence reveals PPC and S1 have complementary neural codes with PPC transforming physical stimulation into conscious perception whereas S1 is more sensitive to stimulus amplitude.

papers.title: Identification of surface colors across environmental illuminations
papers.abstract: When objects are embedded in a complex lighting environment, the illumination they receive depends on their geometric relationship to the environment. We measured performance in an odd-one-out color constancy task, with objects rendered in complex lighting environments. Observers identified the odd object among four objects, with two rendered under each of two lighting environments, sampled from a wide range of object orientations and camera positions. Constancy was high. The presence of a surrounding context increased accuracy. Gloss provided no measurable benefit. We also tested a condition in which the global color impression provided misleading information about the lighting environment, but this impaired performance only slightly. These findings suggest that human color constancy remains robust even under complex lighting environments, contrary to predictions of many simple models of illuminant discounting.

papers.title: Global statistical constraint and local partner-sensitive inference support dynamic, open-ended verbal coordination
papers.abstract: Effective verbal communication requires individuals to align their communicative intentions through the precise use of utterances, yet how this is achieved in dynamic, open-ended communication remains unclear. Combining predictive deep language models (DLMs) with cognitive computational modeling, we tested a computational division of labor between context-sensitive global constraint on the utterance space and partner-sensitive local adjustment of selection priorities. We formalized local adjustment using an active inference inspired updating rule within a statistical-pragmatic hybrid model. Thirty dyads performed a dynamic, open-ended collaborative word-generation task during functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) hyperscanning. Interlocutors converged in their lexical choices, and lexical alignment was best explained by a hybrid model integrating contextual selection priors with interaction-specific local adjustment among the models tested. This hybrid process formed a dynamic hypothesis landscape comprising a global semantic search region and local selection priorities. Critically, interaction did not simply reduce uncertainty: within individuals, the hypothesis space of global semantic search progressively narrowed while local uncertainty among plausible alternatives increased; between partners, both global hypothesis space and local selection became increasingly aligned, with alignment of local selection priorities most strongly predicting subsequent lexical alignment. The contribution of local adjustment was stronger during precise verbal communication than in the control tasks. Neural analyses further identified correlates of the local adjustment process: temporoparietal and anterior temporal regions supported partner-related inference and semantic prediction error, respectively, and their activity during thinking predicted subsequent inferior frontal activity associated with self-updating during speaking. The participant's own hypothesis landscape was also represented in the left inferior parietal-supramarginal cortex. The main findings generalized across language models and an independent Czech dataset. Together, these findings reveal that alignment in open-ended communication emerges from complementary statistical and pragmatic computations, providing a framework for understanding human and human-AI communication.

papers.title: Milk-derived extracellular vesicles are functional mediators of postnatal neuroimmune rescue
papers.abstract: Early parental experiences can be translated into biological signals that are transmitted to offspring. These signals influence developmental trajectories to both increase offspring vulnerability following adverse experiences or promote resilience when environments are supported and enriched. Among the potential routes of parental-offspring communication, milk-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) transferred through nursing are particularly interesting because they carry bioactive molecular cargos capable of influencing recipient cells. Previously, we found that milk-derived EV cargo is remodeled by both adverse and positive experiences and that environmental enrichment (EE) can rescue adversity-associated effects, including EV-miRNA cargo changes. Environmental programming of EVs during lactation may therefore have functional consequences on offspring development and adaptability. Here, we tested whether milk-derived EVs from our rat EE model are sufficient to rescue offspring outcomes following maternal immune activation (MIA). Milk-derived EVs isolated from donor EE dams were administered directly to MIA-exposed pups, mitigating MIA-associated reductions in social behavior. EE-EV administration also promoted social behavior in non-MIA exposed male offspring. To investigate microglia as a cellular target, EE-EVs were administered to LPS-activated BV2 microglial cells. EE-EV exposure attenuated LPS-associated transcriptional alterations across inflammatory pathways, including cytokine, chemokine, and NF-B signaling, while modulating genes associated with cellular homeostasis and metabolic responses. Together, these results 1) support milk-derived EVs as a biologically active interface through which environmental experience may be communicated to offspring, and 2) identify microglial transcriptional responses as a potential cellular pathway underlying these effects.

papers.title: Mapping reward processing circuits: the orbitofrontal-nucleus accumbens white matter pathways and their associations to psychopathological traits
papers.abstract: Dysfunctions in reward circuits, including projections from the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) to the nucleus accumbens (NAcc), have been implicated in psychopathology. The OFC is functionally divided into the medial OFC (mOFC), which processes rewards, and the lateral OFC (lOFC), which responds to non-reward or punishment stimuli. We investigated the structural connectivity of the lOFC-NAcc and mOFC-NAcc pathways and their associations with psychopathological traits using tractography-defined ROI analysis. Diffusion-weighted imaging data from 165 participants (aged 22 - 35, 53% male) in the Human Connectome Project (HCP) were analysed using spherical deconvolution tractography. MegaTrack, a novel tool, enabled tract segmentation via a single manual dissection mapped back to native space. Virtual dissection identified four bilateral pathways connecting the lOFC and mOFC to the NAcc, from which fractional anisotropy (FA) was extracted, and an lOFC/mOFC ratio was computed. Psychopathological traits were measured using HCP Achenbach Adult Self-Report scores. The lOFC-NAcc pathway showed positive associations with psychopathology and the mOFC-NAcc pathway negative associations. The lOFC/mOFC ratio emerged as a stronger predictor than individual pathways, with significant associations for depression, somatic problems, anti-social personality traits, and inattention. Effects were lateralized to the left hemisphere. These findings show that the lOFC-NAcc and mOFC-NAcc pathways can be structurally separated with tractography and display opposing correlations with psychopathological traits in a healthy population. Their ratio may index reward-processing dysfunction, and future research should test whether it is sensitive to dysfunction in clinical populations.

papers.title: Newborns modulate and synchronise their Non-Nutritive Sucking behaviour to the temporal structure of sound
papers.abstract: Sensorimotor synchronization, the ability to align motor behaviour with the temporal structure of external stimuli, is thought to emerge gradually during development, but its origins remain unclear. Here, we investigated whether newborns can adapt their sucking behaviour and synchronise it to the temporal structure of auditory stimuli within the first days of life. Forty-one healthy full-term newborns (24-72 hours old) were exposed to two three-minute auditory streams differing in temporal structure: a highly structured stream with a stable temporal pattern and a highly variant stream with greater temporal variability, while their non-nutritive sucking (NNS) was continuously recorded. We assessed changes in NNS frequency and pressure and quantified NNS-sound coupling using magnitude-squared coherence at frequencies distinctive to each auditory stream. Structured stimulation promoted a more organised NNS, with more suck bursts than the variant stream, and increased sucking vigour, with a transiently higher suck peak rate during the first minute relative to the variant stream and greater suck pressure relative to silence. Coherence analyses revealed that coherence was selectively higher at the frequencies distinctive to each auditory stream, both for the structured and the highly variant stimulus. These findings show that, within hours of birth, NNS behaviour can selectively align with stimulus-specific temporal regularities, even when these are weakly predictable and lack a dominant periodicity. This early capacity to extract temporal structure and coordinate motor behaviour may provide a foundation for the subsequent development of sensorimotor synchronisation.

papers.title: Tonotopic mapping in children shows an overrepresentation of high frequencies in autism
papers.abstract: Altered sensitivity to sounds despite normal peripheral hearing is common in neurodevelopmental disorders but the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we investigate tonotopic organization in 86 children (6-11 years) with autism spectrum and related neurodevelopmental disorders as well as typically developing (TD) peers, using a child-friendly, passive listening, functional magnetic resonance imaging design. In TD children, tonotopic maps in primary auditory cortex resembled the typical high-low-high frequency gradients previously reported in adults, while children with autism showed an overrepresentation of high frequencies consistent with what has been observed in animal models of autism. Higher frequency tuning further correlated with greater caregiver-reported sound but not touch sensitivities. Importantly, tonotopy is a core organizational feature of auditory cortex that develops early in life and remains relatively stable after the critical period of heightened plasticity ends. Thus, these results suggest that atypical auditory processing in autism may result from early disruption to tonotopic map formation. Longitudinal neuroimaging studies are needed to understand the genetic and environmental causes of altered auditory cortex topology and its long-term consequences for higher-level auditory, language, and social communication development.

papers.title: Recruitment of the local GABAergic population engages complex network interactions in the ventral subiculum
papers.abstract: The ventral subiculum (vSub), a major output node of the hippocampal formation, has been implicated in diverse neurological disorders. Disruption of excitatory-inhibitory balance is a common feature of neurological disorders, with altered GABAergic signaling representing a critical component. More recently, the vSub has gained increasing attention as a component of neural circuits underlying emotional and motivational regulation, through its extensive connections with regions implicated in mental health disorders such as addiction and anxiety. Our previous work in models of alcohol use disorder and comorbid anxiety identified an important role for GABAergic inhibition in regulating vSub excitability, prompting us to investigate the functional consequences of recruiting the broader local GABAergic population. Although previous studies have examined individual interneuron subtypes, the network consequences of activating the global population of local GABAergic neurons remain poorly understood. To address this question, we expressed channelrhodopsin using an mDlx-dependent strategy to target GABAergic neurons in the ventral hippocampus and performed in vivo electrophysiological recordings from vSub neurons in anesthetized rats. Repeated activation of this GABAergic population at 20 Hz, a stimulation frequency commonly used in behavioral optogenetic studies, produced robust suppression of pyramidal neuron firing during stimulation. This direct inhibition was accompanied by network-dependent increases in post-stimulus activity that varied as a function of baseline activity, sex, and trial number. Complementary ex vivo electrophysiological experiments further supported network-dependent effects and revealed short-term synaptic plasticity that evolved across repeated stimulation trials, reflecting contributions from both pre- and postsynaptic mechanisms. Together, these findings demonstrate that recruitment of the broader GABAergic population produces effects extending beyond direct inhibition and can engage dynamic network responses that depend on stimulation history and circuit state. These findings highlight the importance of stimulation frequency, timing, and network context when interpreting the functional consequences of GABAergic circuit manipulation.

papers.title: Meis2 is required for GABAergic amacrine cell survival in the developing retina.
papers.abstract: Amacrine cells (ACs) are the most diverse neuron in the retina, with more than sixty different subtypes, each contributing to the detection of specific visual features. Despite their importance in visual feature detection, the genetic basis for this diversity is still not well understood. Recent single-cell transcriptomic datasets have identified several potential genes that may regulate cellular diversity, but the underlying mechanisms have not been investigated. For example, the transcription factor Meis2 is selectively expressed in the GABAergic subclass of ACs. In this study, we focused on how Meis2 regulates the development of GABAergic ACs. We hypothesized that Meis2 is required for specification and survival of GABAergic ACs. To test this, we used the Meis2 conditional knockout mouse (Meis2-CKO) where Meis2 was deleted from either the entire retina or specifically from AC precursor cells. The deletion of Meis2 led to a ~60% reduction in total GABAergic ACs in the retina. This loss of GABAergic ACs occurred only after postnatal day 5 (P5), suggesting Meis2 is not required for early specification but may be required for survival. To further investigate cell death and survival, we quantified cleaved caspase-3 positive cells in the retina at several developmental timepoints. In Meis2-CKO mice, we found an increase in cleaved caspase-3 immunolabeling at P5 and P6 timepoints coinciding with the reduction of GABAergic ACs. Further analysis of GABAergic AC subtypes demonstrated a subtype-specific cell death in Meis2-CKO retinas. For example, the total number of dopaminergic (TH) ACs were significantly reduced, whereas starburst (ChAT) ACs remained unchanged. These findings suggest that Meis2 is important for the survival of a subset of GABAergic AC subtypes in the mammalian retina. In addition, Meis2 may control the expression of specific survival factors that prevent apoptosis during developmental cell death in the retina.

papers.title: Intracellular accumulation of AAV6 genomes governs microglia reactivity and the inflammatory response in retinal gene therapy
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated viral (AAV) vectors possess immense potential for gene therapy applications. However, microglia can mount an immune response against AAV vectors. Yet, microglia are therapeutic targets since they play a driving role in the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. Thus, it is critical to understand the cellular processes driving the microglia-mediated immune response against AAV vectors. To this end, we modelled AAV6 induced inflammation upon retinal gene therapy in minipigs. Upon AAV6 administration, the IBA1+ cells demonstrated a morphological transition to the amoeboid form, indicating microglial reactivity. We also observed the invasion of peripheral immune cells in the retina. To elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms, we transduced human iPSC derived microglia-like cells (iMGLs) in vitro with AAV6 and AAV8 respectively. Only AAV6 transduced iMGLs exhibited morphological features and a transcriptomic signature of microglial reactivity. The magnitude of intracellular AAV6 viral genomes was significantly higher as compared to the AAV8 condition. The elevated levels of intracellular AAV6 genomes induced a DNA damage response in AAV6-transduced iMGLs, which is a key feature of neuroinflammation-linked microglial reactivity. Thus, our work highlights the impact of intracellular viral genome accumulation on microglial reactivity and its implications for retinal gene therapy associated inflammation.

papers.title: Outgrowth of Mouse Sensory Neurons is not Mediated by Regeneration Associated Genes in Early Postnatal Stages
papers.abstract: Peripheral neurons exhibit robust regeneration after nerve injury in adulthood; a process linked to the activation of regeneration-associated genes (RAGs). However, the mechanisms underlying nerve regeneration during early postnatal development remain poorly understood. In a previous work, we observed that motoneurons axotomized at early postnatal stages regenerate without overexpressing RAGs, contrasting with the expected RAG activation observed in postnatal day 30 (P30) mice. To determine whether this phenomenon extends to sensory neurones, we investigated two paradigmatic dorsal root ganglia populations: proprioceptive (PV) and nociceptive (TrpV1) neurones, which exhibit distinct regenerative capacities in adult mice. Following sciatic nerve crush injury at P4, P10, and P30, both neuronal subtypes demonstrated robust axonal regeneration across all postnatal stages, with nociceptors exhibiting significantly superior regeneration compared to proprioceptors. Remarkably, no substantial neuronal death was observed at any developmental timepoint. However, RNA sequencing revealed that P4 and P10 sensory neurones failed to upregulate RAGs following injury, whereas P30 neurones exhibited the expected pro-regenerative transcriptional programme. Pathway enrichment analysis confirmed that classical regeneration-associated signalling pathways were activated exclusively in young adults, whilst developmental and inflammatory pathways predominated in early postnatal stages. Using the conditioning lesion paradigm in primary dorsal root ganglia cultures, we demonstrated that only P30 neurones exhibited enhanced neurite outgrowth following conditioning lesion, whilst P4 and P10 neurones showed no conditioning effect or reduced outgrowth, respectively. These findings indicate that early postnatal sensory neurones possess intrinsic growth capacity independent of RAG activation, suggesting fundamentally distinct regenerative mechanisms across developmental stages.

papers.title: A representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala supports learning and choice
papers.abstract: Animals continuously transform sensory inputs into representations that guide behavior. Although the amygdala is a brain structure critical for learning and choice, how natural sensory experience is represented within this circuit remains unknown. Here, we identify a representation of the visual environment in the human basolateral amygdala (BLA) that contains information relevant for learning and choice. Using image-computable encoding models trained on responses to naturalistic videos, we recover a continuous, low-dimensional representation of visual experience in the BLA. The representation generalizes across individuals and independent datasets and prospectively predicts BLA responses to novel visual stimuli generated through closed-loop image synthesis. Signals derived from the representation also informed reinforcement-learning models of human choice. Together, these findings show that the human BLA organizes complex visual experience into a structured representation that can support learning and flexible behavioral responses.

papers.title: Ultrastructurally planar growth cones during neocortical axon navigation
papers.abstract: Neurons extend axons toward spatially defined but often distant targets to establish brain circuits. Callosal projection neurons exemplify this organization, linking corresponding cortical territories between the two hemispheres. Growing axons rely on growth cones to regulate direction and speed through densely packed tissues. Although growth cone morphology and dynamics have been extensively characterized in cultured neurons and invertebrate models, how growth cones navigate the three-dimensional environment of the developing mammalian brain remains poorly explored. Here, we combined a genetically encoded electron microscopy (EM)-labeling strategy and zero-shot deep-learning-based tracing with high-resolution volume EM to reconstruct growth cones of identified callosal projection neurons in the developing mouse brain. Mediolaterally extending growth cones exhibited a planar, fan-shaped morphology, preferentially expanded along the dorsoventral axis. Filopodia extended from the edges of this plane and aligned predominantly with the same axis but showed no directional bias toward the growing direction. Longitudinal in vivo imaging revealed that increased growth cone complexity associated with filopodial extension coincided with lower instantaneous velocity but preceded accelerated extension. Together, these findings reveal a dorsoventrally oriented planar growth cone architecture in which filopodial extension precedes accelerated axon growth, suggesting a structural constraint that may restrict axon navigation to the callosal plane.

papers.title: Genome-engineered C. elegans strains with sex-transformed neurons and gut
papers.abstract: The sexual identity of specific tissues can be altered through cell-autonomous manipulation of the sex determination pathway in the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans. Previously described sexually mosaic strains carried multicopy transgenic arrays that are potentially subject to transgene silencing or misexpression artefacts. We used here the CRISPR/Cas9 system to engineer strains in which coding sequences for either a masculinizing agent (FEM-3) or a feminizing agent (intracellular domain of TRA-2) are inserted with a trans-splicing system at the 3 end of endogenous genetic loci that are known to be expressed in either a neuron-specific (rab-3) or gut-specific (elt-2) manner. We validate the tissue-specific sex-transformations induced by these genomic manipulations through expression analysis of known sex-specific genes and through assaying behavioral readouts. These strains may serve the worm community as standard reference tools to study the consequences of tissue-specific sex transformations.
